notes: Coverage: every text block, word, ending, accent or absent accent, punctuation, abbreviation, ordinal, and every inline/display formula was compared line by line against both C and H in the assigned half images. This includes all agreed material, not only the loci listed in changes. The whole image was opened once for layout; half_a once, then half_b once. No whole or half image was reopened.

The view record and each crop timestamp report actual tool openings. Each of the 17 stored crops was inspected once. Adjacent open loci share the dateline crop, the first-display crop, or the single rotated marginal-note crop; no decided locus was recropped. Crop pixel boxes are in the stated source half image, not in the enlarged output.

This is a handwritten letter page with a dateline, Cher Deligne salutation, a long prose paragraph, a two-row brace display, a three-object arrow diagram labelled (T), and a sideways left-margin note. It has no visible signature, closing, author page number, title or page total. The lower-left archive number is 8; H’s page{8} is credited as matching metadata, not an omission.

Hand identities are not established by this packet. The main text, faded dateline and marginal ink are described conservatively. The pencil-like archive numeral is a separate physical layer. The page is wholly handwritten, so no global handwritten wrapper was used.

The letter says a leg may prevent the writer from giving a first-cycle course in the first trimester, and proposes a small algebra seminar on the material of Mme Sinh, perhaps transposed to the context of double-quoted champs. The word ma/une, clipped course-word ending, clipped character after peut-être, small name abbreviation and part of éventuellement remain source uncertainties.

The page itself qualifies the following observation as remaining heuristique. It introduces E(M,N) by a truncated derived-Hom expression for two abelian sheaves on a topos X, writes its two cohomology conditions and says there should be a canonical distinguished triangle. No proof or computation is written on this page, and none was independently supplied here.

The literal first comparison sign and second H exponent were checked because they differ from the inequality/index suggested by the adjacent conditions. The resulting readings 0=i≤2 and H^j with a condition on i are transcription decisions from the ink, not mathematical repairs. No theorem or cohomological assertion was checked or proved in this run; math_checks is intentionally empty.

The single overwritten name in the first invariant row is preserved as a deletion/covered layer plus the live Ext. No independent caret insertion, separate marginal pointer, cancelled paragraph or non-diagram drawing was found. Long returning strokes under Deligne, algèbre, envisage, triangle and distingué belong to handwritten descenders, rather than independent emphasis underlines.

The marginal note has no visible attachment sign. It is retained as a marginal note without inventing a caret. Its first line is clipped along the tops of the letters; the second line que tu cites is substantially preserved but has an ambiguous high stroke near the final e. The one rotated crop records that uncertainty in place.

H’s historical/editorial assertions about other material, its cited verification and its note about another letter copy were not used as visual evidence and are not copied into the diplomatic page. The visible date digits 7.8.74 are clear; the preceding faded remnant does not establish a complete 2.

Differences settled directly in the halves have empty crop_ids and explicitly say which half settled them. They are available for the main reader’s required independent adjudication crops. Macro-name substitutions alone were not counted as reading differences.
